ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$10.67 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (metered extra distance on the unexempted off-route/stationary segment) and note the RD-1 breach on the driver's record; no account flag warranted.

segment_findings.reason: Rider asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming a location (17:33:25) and the driver accepted ('Ok', 17:33:55); the chat messages carry timestamps and predate the stop, so RD-5 consent to this specific route change is absent. Under RD-3(b) the driver unilaterally chose a store ~1.3 km off the optimal PIE corridor (trace 1.31349,103.88838 vs route 1.3224,103.88758) and did not tell the rider the location beforehand, so the extra distance is not exempted; RD-3(c) only makes the ~4.5 min stop time chargeable. RD-4 does not exempt: no traffic incidents and the PIE band is 4, not band 1–2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's 'the rider asked for a 7-Eleven stop ... I went to the one I know' does not establish consent to the off-route choice: RD-5 requires the rider's own pre-detour message agreeing to that route change, and only the location-less stop request is in the chat (G11).
